concepts.name: What back-of-envelope means
concepts.summary: Quick, rounded arithmetic from stated assumptions and common performance numbers (Jeff Dean's definition) that aims for the right order of magnitude, to judge which designs can meet the requirements.

concepts.name: Round, state assumptions, label units
concepts.summary: Round to powers of 10 while calculating (1 day ≈ 10^5 s, 1M/day ≈ 10/s), write every assumption down, and put a unit on every number.

concepts.name: QPS and peak QPS from DAU
concepts.summary: Average QPS = DAU x requests per user per day ÷ 10^5; peak QPS = average x a stated peak factor (2x-10x); compute reads and writes separately to see the read:write ratio.

concepts.name: Storage estimate
concepts.summary: Storage = item size x new items per day x days retained x copies; estimate item size from its fields, and do not apply the peak factor to storage.

concepts.name: Bandwidth estimate
concepts.summary: Bandwidth = peak QPS x payload per request, in and out separately; network links are quoted in bits, so multiply bytes per second by 8.

concepts.name: Latency orders of magnitude
concepts.summary: RAM is ~100 ns, an SSD random read ~150 µs, a same-datacenter round trip ~0.5 ms, an HDD seek ~10 ms and a cross-region round trip 50-150 ms; know the ranking and the gaps, not the digits.

concepts.name: Powers of two and data units
concepts.summary: Every 10 powers of two is about 1,000: 2^10 ≈ KB, 2^20 ≈ MB, 2^30 ≈ GB, 2^40 ≈ TB, 2^50 ≈ PB; 2^32 ≈ 4.3 billion.

concepts.name: Availability in nines
concepts.summary: Each extra nine cuts downtime 10x (99.9% ≈ 8.8 h/year, 99.99% ≈ 53 min/year); components in sequence multiply availability down, components in parallel raise it.

concepts.name: What one component can handle
concepts.summary: Modern rough limits: a SQL database up to ~50K transactions/s and a few TB per instance, Redis 100K+ ops/s, an app server 100K+ connections; older tables quote far lower numbers.

concepts.name: From estimate to decision
concepts.summary: Put each estimate next to a component's limit: under it, keep one box; reads far above writes point to caching and replicas; tens of TB or 10K+ writes/s point to splitting data; petabytes of files point to object storage.

concepts.name: When to estimate
concepts.summary: Estimate the numbers that can change a decision, when they are needed; skip or shorten estimates that only conclude 'it's a lot'. Sources disagree on doing it upfront.
